claim.value: Persistent backlogs can obscure the attachment response to the responsibility change.
claim.scope: Interpretation of the prospective before-and-after attachment comparison.

provenance.rationale: P026 states the potential masking effect of persistent backlogs; P009 identifies the comparison whose response is being interpreted.

signal_basis.value: Compare missing-attachment frequency across comparable covered orders before and after responsibility becomes explicit, using consistent inspection intervals. The proposed signal is a reduction, repeated across comparable periods if volume permits; interpretation must distinguish new orders from backlog repairs.
signal_basis.scope: Prospective attachment-frequency comparison following clarification of responsibility.

provenance.rationale: The cited spans supply the comparison, proposed reduction, repetition qualifier, inspection timing and distinction between new orders and backlog repairs.
No unresolved empirical relation is required for this bounded possibility claim.

rationale: Persistent missing attachments from older orders can remain despite improvement in new orders, obscuring that improvement when interpreting attachment frequencies. This licenses the stated possibility and the distinction between new orders and backlog repairs.
uncertainty: The claim does not establish that backlogs actually obscured this comparison or quantify any masking effect.
